mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median rank IC falls below 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and depresses equity prices over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered quarters, or the mechanism fails when unemployment is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 0.4 percentage points signals a tightening labor market that elevates wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of triggered months, or the effect reverses when inflation is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below -0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong consumer spending growth.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST below their prior 12-month averages signals broad-based weakness in economic activity and housing demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 12mo avg AND HOUST < 12mo avg in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 yields positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of triggered months, or the effect is not statistically significant after controlling for monetary policy shocks.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of higher rates and inflation, which increases discount rates and erodes real earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12mo avg AND CPIAUCSL > 12mo avg in the same month
regime_hint: high inflation and restrictive monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered quarters, or the effect is not robust during periods of strong global growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in PAYEMS above 0.3% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month + 0.3% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered months, or the effect disappears when wage growth is stagnant.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in RSAFS below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals weakening consumer savings and spending capacity, which reduces demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12mo SMA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not present during periods of rising credit availability.
